extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on grounds and form paragraphs to reject or object to patent claims (chiefly 35 U.S.C. §112 second paragraph indefiniteness, new matter, duplicate/omnibus claims, disclaimer, foreign-filing bars, res judicata, reissue limits, and procedures for final/previously-allowed rejections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — Failure to claim applicant's invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as failing to set forth the subject matter which applicant(s) regard as their invention (evidence found in applicant reply/statements indicating the invention differs from what is defined in the claim(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. Use only where applicant has stated (outside the application as filed) that the invention is different from the claims (e.g., in remarks, brief, affidavit). In bracketed text explain applicant submission, what applicant stated, and how that statement indicates a different invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — Indefinite (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. Follow with one or more specific form paragraphs 7.34.02–7.34.11 as applicable; if none fit, supply a full explanation identifying particular term(s)/limitations causing indefiniteness and why. If one skilled in the art could determine scope, this rejection is not appropriate. See MPEP §§ 2171–2174. Use form paragraph 7.34.15 for pro se applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology redefinition inconsistent with accepted meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant acts as own lexicographer to redefine a claim term contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the term to put one skilled in the art on notice of the uncommon definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the meaning assigned by the claim and the accepted meaning. Support examiner's accepted meaning with appropriate references (textbook/dictionary) per MPEP § 2173.05(a). This paragraph must be preceded by 7.34.01 and used only where the specification does not clearly redefine the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative term / term of degree rendering claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term or term of degree (e.g., 'sufficient', 'substantial') that is not defined by the claim or specification and provides no standard for ascertaining the requisite degree renders the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which parameter, quantity, or limitation is rendered indefinite and why. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad range and narrow range/limitation within same claim (indefiniteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that recites a broad range/limitation together with a narrow range/limitation that falls within the broad range (in the same claim) is indefinite because it fails to clearly set forth the metes and bounds of protection desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the broader and narrower recitations and where they appear. May be modified to fit other indefiniteness instances. Must be preceded by 7.34.01. See MPEP § 2173.05(c) and cited Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of antecedent basis in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] recites limitation [2] in [3], but there is insufficient antecedent basis for that limitation in the claim (e.g., 'said lever' without introducing 'a lever').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes claim scope indeterminate. Identify the limitation and where it appears (line or paragraph). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claims that merely recite a use without steps (indefinite / non-proper process)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that provides for the use of [2] but does not set forth steps involved in the method/process is unclear and indefinite; mere recital of a use can render the claim improper as a process claim under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert what is being 'used' and explain deficiency. See MPEP § 2173.05(q) and cited cases. Must be preceded by 7.34.01. If the claim recites a use only, consider rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 as not a proper process claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are literal translation (grammatical/idiomatic defects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that are generally narrative and indefinite because they are literal translations from a foreign document and contain grammatical and idiomatic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out that claims fail to conform with current U.S. practice. This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite claim language: 'for example'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'for example' in a claim can render it indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite claim language: 'or the like'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'or the like' renders claim(s) indefinite since it encompasses elements not actually disclosed, making claim scope unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite claim language: 'such as'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'such as' renders a claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifier of 'means' lacks function (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'means' is preceded by words that do not convey a function (e.g., 'conduit means'), no function is specified and it is impossible to determine equivalents as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words preceding 'means' must convey a function (e.g., 'latch means' conveys 'latching'). If the phrase can be restated as 'means for ____' and still make sense, it's definite. Must be preceded by 7.34.01. See Ex parte Klumb and examples in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential steps omitted (method claims incomplete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for omitting essential steps such that there is a gap between steps; omitted steps are [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. Give rationale for considering omitted steps critical/essential and list the omitted steps in bracketed text. See MPEP § 2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential elements omitted (device claims incomplete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for omitting essential elements such that there is a gap between elements; omitted elements are [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. Give rationale for why omitted elements are critical/essential and list them. See MPEP § 2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential cooperative relationships omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, amounting to a gap between necessary structural connections; omitted relationships are [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. Explain why omitted structural cooperative relationships are critical/essential and identify them. See MPEP § 2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 for pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims by pro se applicants that are narrative, indefinite, and functional/operational in language are rejected for failing to define the invention as required; structure must be clearly and positively specified and claims must be in one-sentence form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.34.15 for pro se applicants. Note format of exemplary patent claims and specify that structure must present a complete operative device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus claim (fails to point out included/excluded matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as an omnibus-type claim failing to point out what is included or excluded (e.g., 'A device substantially as shown and described').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. Use this paragraph to reject an omnibus-type claim; no further explanation necessary. See MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation by examiner's amendment upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or trade name used as claim limitation (indefiniteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a trademark/trade name in a claim to identify or describe a material/product does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph because trademarks identify source, not goods, making claim scope uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the trademark/trade name and where used; specify the material/product the trademark is meant to identify/describe. Cite Ex parte Simpson. This form paragraph addresses indefiniteness caused by trademark usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate claims — warning and objection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates or so close in content that they cover the same thing despite slight wording differences, object to the duplicate under 37 CFR 1.75 after allowing one claim (use form paragraphs 7.05.05 for warning; 7.05.06 for objection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.05.05 when duplicate claims are present and not allowable to give applicant chance to correct. If one claim is allowable, object the duplicate with 7.05.06. See MPEP § 706.03(k) and § 804 for double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter — objection under 35 U.S.C. 132(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that introduce subject matter not disclosed in the original application are objectionable as 'new matter' (35 U.S.C. 132(a)); new matter may include added specific percentages/compounds or omission of method steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect and object to new matter in abstracts, specification, or drawings using Form Paragraph 7.28; if new matter is added to claims, also reject under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (use form paragraph 7.31.01). Identify new matter by page/line/drawing figure, require applicant to cancel new matter in reply, and consider added matter as part of claimed subject matter for other rejections/priors. See MPEP §§ 2163.05–2163.07 and § 608.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing without license (35 U.S.C. 182–185) — abandonment/bar to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Unauthorized filing of an application in a foreign country prior to six months after U.S. filing (or without license) may constitute abandonment of the invention or bar patenting; similar statutory rules apply for inventions under secrecy orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner learns of corresponding foreign application filed before the U.S. application was on file for six months and the invention was made here, refer the application to Licensing and Review Section (TC work group 3640). Pending investigation, application may be returned to TC for prosecution on the merits. Licensing and Review will request transfer if action under 35 U.S.C. 185 is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer-based rejection (failure to present claims for interference / failure to appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be made where applicant has disclaimed subject matter by failing to present claims for interference, failing to copy claims when suggested, or failing to respond/appeal within required times; such disclaimers can apply to all claims not patentably distinct from disclaimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.48 (failure to present claims for interference) and 7.49 (rejection for failure to appeal/adverse judgment entered by Board). 7.48 should be used only after applicant was notified that interference proceedings are required and refused to copy claims. Specify the statutory basis (e.g., 102(g) or 102(g)/103(a) as appropriate) and include examiner's basis for obviousness when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata as a ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may justify rejection when an earlier decision by the Board or a reviewing court involved the same claim or issue and there is no opportunity for further court review of the earlier decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply res judicata only in appropriate circumstances; ordinarily also act on the basis of prior art. Cite relevant cases sustaining or reversing res judicata rejections and apply cautiously. See MPEP discussion and cited precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application limitations (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids granting a reissue that enlarges the scope of claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from grant; reissue by assignee is limited and claims enlarging scope may be rejected as barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue is applied for within two years (or properly claims benefit), examiner need not consider undue delay. Defective reissue oath may be ground to reject all reissue claims. See MPEP Chapter 1400 and cited cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of previously allowed claims — procedural safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall be rejected thereafter only after the proposed rejection is submitted to the primary examiner for consideration and approval; give full faith and credit to prior examiner's search/action unless clear error or new art is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise great care before rejecting a previously allowed claim. Use Form Paragraph 7.50 when withdrawing indicated allowability in view of newly discovered reference(s); any such action requires Primary Examiner signature. See Ex parte Grier and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection — requirements and reply limitations (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: On second or subsequent examination, the examiner may make a rejection final; the final rejection must repeat or state all grounds of rejection and clearly state reasons supporting rejections; applicant's reply is limited to appeal or specified amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing a final rejection, develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant. In a final rejection, the examiner must state all applicable grounds and reasons. Replies to a final action must include cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim; if any claim stands allowed the reply must comply with form requirements. See 37 CFR 1.113 and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing and usage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs must be preceded by specified other form paragraphs (e.g., most 7.34.xx paragraphs must be preceded by 7.34.01 or 7.30.02/7.103); appropriate sequencing and selection of form paragraphs is required when drafting Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examiner notes about mandatory precedences and exclusivity (e.g., 7.30.01/7.30.02 used only once in a given action; some paragraphs only to be used where specification does not redefine a term). When no form paragraph fits, supply a full, explicit explanation of the claim deficiency.
